feed.title: Amazon files FCC application for 5,105 direct-to-device satellites
feed.summary: Amazon has filed an application with the FCC to launch 5,105 low Earth orbit satellites for direct-to-device connectivity, with deployment expected to begin in 2028. This system, part of the Amazon Leo Direct-to-Device initiative, aims to provide voice, messaging, data, and emergency services to areas outside cellular coverage, leveraging spectrum from its planned acquisition of Globalstar. The service will partner with mobile network operators and operate alongside existing Globalstar and Amazon Leo broadband constellations.

feed.title: Why market volatility may be part of the bull case
feed.summary: Market volatility, while often seen negatively, can actually be a component of a healthy bull market. Periods of doubt and pullbacks can reset and extend market cycles, as evidenced by the "Magnificent 7" stocks and the broader S&P 500, which have seen highs continue to get higher despite setbacks. Skepticism surrounding AI investments is natural but doesn't signify a deteriorating investment thesis, as the structural bull market remains intact, supported by early-stage investment themes and a resilient economy.

feed.title: Amazon files for 5,105-satellite direct-to-device network using Globalstar spectrum
feed.summary: Amazon's Kuiper Systems has applied to the FCC for permission to launch a new 5,105-satellite low Earth orbit constellation designed for direct-to-device connectivity using Globalstar's mobile-satellite spectrum. The approach differs from Starlink and AST SpaceMobile by utilizing spectrum already allocated for mobile-satellite service, rather than relying on the FCC's Supplemental Coverage from Space framework.
